query: I'm looking for a workout bench that is easy to assemble and feels solid without wobbling. Can you provide tips on how to avoid issues during assembly, like handling the bolts and washers? Also, what should I do if I can't find the allen wrench needed for assembly? Finally, how can I ensure that I don't accidentally stack washers when putting it together? For my workouts with dumbbells, I need something reliable and durable that fits my budget.
ori_review:
The bench assembled easily and feels solid with no wobbling. My first work out with the new bench went well. I'll only work out with dumbbells, so I don't envision any issues in terms of weight loads.

A few recommendations...

1. Be careful when opening the shipping box. The package that contains the bolts and washers had opened in transit. Had I opened the box in the wrong area, it could have been a bear to find the washers after they spilled out. Fortunately, I opened the shipping box on the living room carpet, so it was easy to corral the runaway washers.

2. Do not tighten any of the bolts until you have all of the bolts in and they've begun to thread. You have to jiggle things a bit to get all holes lined up. If you tighten things down ahead of time, you won't be able to jiggle the pieces enough to get all of the bolts threaded.

3. There is an allen wrench provided in the shipment. (It was the only tool I needed to complete the assembly.) At first, I didn't see it and thought I'd have to head to the store to buy a metric allen wrench to tighten the bolts, but as I rummaged through the packaging material, the allen wrench appeared. I'm not sure if it was in the same package as the bolts and washers and had broken free, or if it was free swimming in the box. Anyway, it is there, so keep an eye out for it.

4. The washers tend to cling to one another, so it is easy to put two washers on a bolt and not notice. I ended up thinking I was two washers short as I was ready to put the last two bolts into place. On closer examination, I noticed two of the partially inserted bolts had two washers on them.

For the price and for my purpose, it fits the bill.

query: I'm looking for an easy and cost-effective way to regrip my golf clubs. I've had my clubs for around 10 years, and the grips are in bad shape. Can you guide me on how to use a grip kit effectively, including what additional supplies I might need, like solvent, and any tips for the regripping process? I want to ensure I do it right and have a good experience when playing with the new grips.
ori_review:
I'm not one of those golfers that buy a new set of clubs every year or so, and, after 10 years, the grips on my clubs were in bad shape. I purchased the Golf Pride kit and was able to completely re-grip my set of clubs in a couple of hours. The kit contains 13 grips (you need a different kind of grip for your putter), grip tape and a rubber vice grip (so you won't scratch your club when placing it in a vice). It does not include the grip solvent, which I purchased at a local golf shop earlier when I re-gripped my putter. The instructions tell you about other solvents you can use that can be purchased in a hardware store.

The process is easy:
- Remove the old grip and tape (I used a utility knife but be careful not to scratch the shaft) - be sure all the old tape is removed;
- Place the rubber vice grip on the shaft and place the club in the vice;
- Remove the plastic label from the new grip;
- Apply the tape to the end of the shaft, leaving about 1/4 inch or so overlap on the end (it makes it easier to start the grip on the shaft). The tape is double-sided, so you peel off one side, apply it to the shaft, and then peel off the other side;
- Apply the solvent to the tape - I just applied it to the top and used a finger to spread it out. This makes the tape slippery, activating the glue. Use plenty of solvent so the tape is very slippery.
- Place some solvent inside the grip itself and be sure the inside is coated;
- Finally, with the grip's label where you want it, slide the grip on the tape until it's completely on the club. You have a few seconds to position the logo as you want it.
- Set the club on the floor grip down to drain any solvent that might be remaining.

That's all there is to it. I played a round the next day with new grips and it felt great.
